item.title: One Loss Resolves Signed Rank-One Gradient Fibers: Exact Decoding on Cycle and Theta Blocks
item.description: arXiv:2610.35531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For masked rank-one least squares with unrestricted signs, gradients reveal weighted margins and the loss reveals the target's squared norm. We prove that this one scalar resolves the gradient ambiguity on bipartite cycle and length-three parallel-path blocks: every target fixed before sampling and nonzero on cycle edges is identified almost surely by one legal positive query drawn from an absolutely continuous law. On six-cycle flowers, open target and query sets retain $3^r$ bounded gradient candidates. A common algebraic witness excludes cross-block energy cancellation. Cactus masks admit explicit exception certificates and target-uniform finite-grid bounds; theta blocks admit an existence guarantee. For nondegenerate cactus reductions, an exact decoder returns complete actual real lists, with bit cost polynomial in input length, the cycle-degree product $D$ and the optional budget parameter $2^\kappa$. Energy-coordinate propagation certifies singletons without a product join. The product $D$ can grow exponentially in cycle count. Exponential certificate-degree and output bounds, and weak NP-hardness at a fixed uniform query, characterize distinct costs of exact decoding.
item.dc:creator: Junwen Lou, Shuo Tian, Penghui Liu

item.title: Proceedings Twelfth International Conference on Non-Classical Logics. Theory and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.34489v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Non-Classical Logics. Theory and Applications (NCL) is an international conference aimed at presenting novel results and survey papers in the broad field of non-classical logics and their applications. The first two editions were held in {\L}{\'o}d{\'z}, Poland, in September 2008 and 2009. Subsequent editions were organised in Toru{\'n} (2010, 2012, 2015, 2018) and {\L}{\'o}d{\'z} (2011, 2013, 2016, 2022, 2024). The tenth edition of the conference, organised by the University of {\L}{\'o}d{\'z} in 2022, was the first to have its proceedings published in EPTCS. We are honoured and pleased to continue this practice and, for the third time, include all accepted long papers in an EPTCS volume. Furthermore, for the first time, we have also included all accepted extended abstracts in the volume.
item.dc:creator: Andrzej Indrzejczak (University of {\L}{\'o}d{\'z}, Poland), Tomasz Jarmu{\.z}ek (Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toru{\'n}, Poland), Mateusz Klonowski (Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toru{\'n}, Poland), Micha{\l} Zawidzki (University of {\L}{\'o}d{\'z}, Poland)

item.title: NeSySpec: Neuro-Symbolic Technical Intelligence for Auditing Engineering Specifications with an Application to Aircraft
item.description: arXiv:2610.35403v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Engineers who audit a declared specification of an engineered system need to know which physical constraints it respects, which it violates, which field was altered and how to correct it. NeSySpec is an integrated and interpretable neuro-symbolic audit framework, built on Logic Tensor Networks, that answers these questions in one pipeline. Its axioms encode the physical relations of the domain as differentiable graded predicates whose tolerances are learned from a fleet of real records; from the same degrees, it diagnoses the violated constraint, identifies the altered field by abduction, proposes a minimum-change correction and ties image evidence to the parts it describes, abstaining exactly where evidence is missing, and returns all of it in one verification report. We validate NeSySpec on 107 aircraft types, with 16 test aircraft of 9 families held out of training, on specification records paired with ground photographs and satellite imagery and on synthetic errors: generated corruptions, edits labeled from the edit alone and deliberate falsifications. NeSySpec combines all the assessed audit outputs in one pipeline, which no learned, rule-based, solver-based, neuro-symbolic or language-model comparator does; on the test aircraft none is ahead of it in the macro-F1 of its constraint verdicts, in naming the violated constraint and the altered field or in the repair error, and it is competitive in record and image-pair detection. Its diagnosis names the violated constraint in 94.2% of corrupted test records, against 79.5% for classical Fellegi-Holt diagnosis, and on edits labeled from the edit alone, without retraining, abduction finds the altered field in 59.3% of records, against 30.6% for minimum-cardinality localization with random tie- breaking. Only the knowledge base, the visual predicates, the corruption generator and the data are specific to the domain.
item.dc:creator: Pier Mattia Basciano, Gianvito Antenori, Cristiano Andolfi, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone

item.title: Certified bounds on optimization problems in quantum theory
item.description: arXiv:2512.17713v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Semidefinite relaxations of polynomial optimization have become a central tool for addressing the non-convex optimization problems over non-commutative operators that are ubiquitous in quantum information theory and, more in general, quantum physics. Yet, as these global relaxation methods are solved numerically, the bounds issued by the semidefinite solver can - and often do - exceed the global optimum, undermining their certifiability. To counter this issue, we introduce a framework for extracting rigorous certified bounds on non-commutative optimization problems from inexact numerical data, and apply it to several paradigmatic problems in quantum information theory. An extension to sparsity and symmetry-adapted semidefinite relaxations is also provided and compared to the general dense scheme. Our results establish rational post-processing as a practical route to reliable certification, pushing semidefinite optimization toward a certifiable standard for quantum information science.
item.dc:creator: Younes Naceur, Jie Wang, Victor Magron, Antonio Ac\'in

item.title: SRHarness: A Harness for Agentic Symbolic Regression
item.description: arXiv:2609.35501v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent agentic symbolic regression approaches increasingly rely on large language models to analyze data, select scientific operations, and refine hypotheses over long search trajectories. In such systems, performance depends not only on the underlying model and search strategy, but also on the runtime infrastructure that supports scientific search. We introduce SRHarness, a domain-specific harness for agentic symbolic regression built around three mechanisms: composable scientific actions that provide a common interface over raw, transformed, and candidate-derived quantities; persistent scientific state that retains evaluated hypotheses and exposes compact model-facing views; and trajectory lifecycle management that coordinates continuation, branching, restart, and termination. On LLM-SRBench, SRHarness consistently improves both numerical generalization and symbolic recovery under matched LLM backbones. With DeepSeek-v4-flash-0731, it achieves 93.69% symbolic accuracy on LSR-Transform, compared with 62.16% for SR-Scientist, and retains 72.97% accuracy on an anonymized variant that removes scientific descriptions and variable semantics, versus 39.64% for SR-Scientist. Under the same DeepSeek-v4-flash-0731 backbone, SRHarness also substantially outperforms Codex (72.97% vs. 20.72%) and reaches performance comparable to Codex with GPT-5.5, while simply providing Codex with the same scientific tools does not reproduce this advantage. These results show that effective agentic symbolic regression depends not only on models or tools, but also on structured runtime support for organizing scientific actions, accumulated hypotheses, and long-horizon search.
item.dc:creator: Zihan Yu, Shixuan Zhou, Hao Huang, Jingtao Ding, Yong Li
